endpoint_separation.rule: A near-saturated diagnostic may not veto the primary endpoint. Diagnostics explain the mechanism; they do not define the hypothesis.

headroom_normalized_endpoint.definition: HCR = (m1 - m0) / (1 - m0), the fraction of remaining error closed
headroom_normalized_endpoint.rule: if m0 >= 0.95: require m1 >= m0 - 0.02 (saturation clause) else: require HCR >= 0.15
headroom_normalized_endpoint.why: v1 required an ABSOLUTE +0.05 from a baseline of 0.80-0.96, so at most 0.04-0.20 of headroom existed and a near-saturated diagnostic could veto overwhelming primary-endpoint gains. Headroom closure is scale-correct across baselines. This is a reformulation of an ill-posed criterion, NOT a relaxed threshold: +0.05 absolute on an 0.80 baseline is HCR 0.25, whereas the new bar is HCR 0.15 -- lower in headroom terms, and explicitly justified before any v2 number exists.
